node-1.label: 17-year-old male presented with 3 days of mouth pain and nonpainful penile erosions

node-2.label: One week prior, he experienced transient anosmia and ageusia that spontaneously resolved; he denied fever, cough, dyspnea, rhinorrhea, and gastrointestinal symptoms

node-3.label: Physical examination showed afebrile status with normal vital signs (respiratory rate 16 breaths per minute, oxygen saturation 97%); shallow erosions of the vermilion lips and hard palate, circumferential erythematous erosions of the periurethral glans penis, and 5 small vesicles on the trunk and upper extremities; palms, soles, cervical lymphatic, and cardiopulmonary examinations were unremarkable

node-4.label: He had taken acetaminophen and ibuprofen before presenting to the emergency department, but no medications before the onset of the mucocutaneous eruption

why.why: Repeated positive SARS-CoV-2 PCR confirms recent COVID-19, and negative respiratory pathogen testing supports a viral rather than atypical bacterial cause. The afebrile status, normal vital signs, and absence of medication before onset favor a post-viral exanthem. However, HSV PCR, VZV/enterovirus panels, and Tzanck/dermatopathology are unavailable, so other viral etiologies cannot be fully excluded, limiting confidence to 0.80.

Although positive SARS-CoV-2 PCR confirms a recent viral infection, the afebrile status, normal vital signs, and lack of any medication before symptom onset favor a post-viral exanthem over SJS/EM. Negative respiratory pathogen testing reduces the likelihood of an atypical bacterial trigger, so confidence is lowered to 0.08.

Repeated positive SARS-CoV-2 PCR confirms recent COVID-19, and the transient anosmia/ageusia is more consistent with a viral upper respiratory infection than with syphilis/HSV. HSV PCR is unavailable, so HSV cannot be completely excluded, but the absence of fever, normal vital signs, and atypical prodrome keep the likelihood low at 0.06.

Positive SARS-CoV-2 PCR supports an infectious viral process, and the transient anosmia/ageusia and scattered skin vesicles are atypical for Behçet disease. No new evidence supports a systemic autoimmune cause, so confidence is reduced to 0.03.
